summary.en: Choose integer, character, floating or Boolean types and measure their implementation-dependent sizes.
summary.bn: পূর্ণসংখ্যা, অক্ষর, ভগ্নাংশ বা বুলিয়ান টাইপ বেছে নাও এবং বাস্তবায়ননির্ভর আকার মাপো।

notes: _Bool and stdbool.h were added in C99. In C17, bool, true and false are header macros; in C23 they are language keywords. The course's Boolean example uses the C17 header form. Basic integer and floating type sizes remain implementation-dependent.

examQuestions.question: Why should sizeof results be printed with %zu, and what is guaranteed about sizeof(char)?
examQuestions.answerHtml: sizeof returns size_t, an unsigned integer type whose portable output format is %zu. sizeof(char) is always one C byte. The number of bits in a byte is CHAR_BIT, at least eight, so one byte does not universally imply eight bits.

examQuestions.question: Choose types for a grade, whole-number marks, CGPA and readiness flag, and discuss floating-point precision.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
A char can store a grade character, int can hold bounded whole-number marks, double can represent an approximate CGPA, and bool from stdbool.h can hold a C17 readiness flag. Confirm required ranges rather than assuming universal byte sizes. Integers are exact within their range, while binary floating-point approximates many decimal fractions; 0.1 + 0.2 can reveal rounding at high output precision. Displaying two decimal places does not make the stored arithmetic exact.

Marking: four type choices 2, implementation limits 1, precision explanation 2.

examQuestions.question: Write a complete C program for this lab task: Read roll 0 to 9999, grade character and CGPA 0 to 4; print Input: then R C V on one line, CGPA to two decimals.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int roll;
    char grade;
    double cgpa;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %c %lf", &roll, &grade, &cgpa) != 3) {
        return 1;
    }
    printf("%d %c %.2f\n", roll, grade, cgpa);
    return 0;
}

Marking: 1 for typed declarations, 1 for checked input, 2 for the required calculation or transformation, and 1 for exact output.
